ops.new_text: \paragraph{Closest benchmark.} Filice et al.~\cite{lookingbeyond2026} evaluate frozen ECG foundation models as feature extractors on four 12-lead datasets, PTB-XL among them. The models are ECG-FM, ECGFounder, HuBERT-ECG in three sizes and the ECG-JEPA of Weimann and Conrad. Beside classifier probes under class-balanced 15-fold cross-validation, they report the ARI of Gaussian-mixture clusters of the embeddings. They find that ECGFounder and ECG-FM separate their embeddings more by clinical label than by dataset, while HuBERT-ECG and ECG-JEPA separate them more by dataset than by label. Their benchmark compares foundation models with one another. It includes no hand-crafted baseline and does not use MIT-BIH. This study adds both. It also reads each clustering score against a supervised ceiling, computed with patient-grouped five-fold cross-validation on the same records and representation. A low clustering score can then be attributed to geometry or to missing information.
